name: Andromeda Galaxy
headline: diameter
subtitle: Messier 31
description: The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) is the nearest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, about 2.5 million light-years away. NASA estimates it at roughly 220,000 to 260,000 light-years across, well over twice the commonly quoted width of our own galaxy's disc. From a dark site it is visible to the unaided eye, and its angular size is about six times that of the full Moon.

measures.label: Diameter (estimated)
measures.note: Estimated: 'some 220,000 light-years wide' (NASA) to 260,000 light-years for the whole galaxy/disc (NASA GALEX, NASA Space Place)

facts.text: At about 2.5 million light-years away, Andromeda is the Milky Way's largest galactic neighbour; in NASA's Galaxy Evolution Explorer ultraviolet image the entire galaxy spans 260,000 light-years.
NASA Space Place gives the disc of Andromeda as about 260,000 light-years, compared with about 100,000 light-years for the Milky Way's disc.
In angular size Andromeda appears about six times the apparent diameter of the full Moon; a 2025 Hubble panorama of it needed over 600 overlapping snapshots.

sources.title: Our Milky Way Galaxy: How Big is Space?
The Andromeda Galaxy - Across the Spectrum (poster)

caveats: All sizes are estimated. The galaxy has no sharp edge, and the figure depends on the wavelength and how far out the faint disc is traced.
No NASA or ESA page fetched gives Andromeda's mass in a unit the site supports, so mass is left out.
